issues.problem: A reflector forwards each beam it receives synchronously and immediately. The Laser Interface relays only receiveLaser(long,long,long), so the beam age is lost. If a reflector points at a Laser Interface synchronized to that same reflector, the beam re-enters with age 0 every time. The result is unbounded recursion (StackOverflowError) on the server. Also, two beams arriving in the same tick are forwarded separately rather than as one merged beam, so the age>=10 maximum-merge rule never reaches the downstream receiver.
issues.reason: A loop the player can build crashes the server, and the reflector does not output the merged laser the original rules call for.
issues.fix: Override receiveLaser(LaserBeam, Direction) in InterfaceBlockEntity so it relays the LaserBeam with its age. Make the reflector accumulate the beams received during a tick with LaserBeam.merge and emit the merged beam once from its serverTick instead of delivering recursively inside receiveLaser.

issues.reason: The emission direction and the reflector orientation shown in the world disagree with the actual beam direction and hitbox, which fails the 向き/反射 display requirement.
issues.fix: Swap the vertical rotations (UP -> x=270, DOWN -> x=90) and regenerate the blockstates with runData.

issues.problem: Every beam is centered on its block's center line and its half-width depends only on the component sum. Two crossing beams of the same strength at the same height, like the red/green pair in clay-lasers.mjs, have top and bottom faces in exactly the same plane inside the crossing square, which causes z-fighting.
issues.reason: The AC explicitly requires no z-fighting at the crossing point, and the approach calls for a z-fighting countermeasure.
issues.fix: Give each beam axis a slightly different half-width or offset (e.g. a small per-axis epsilon) so faces of perpendicular beams are never coplanar.

issues.problem: The emitter saves the derived runtime state irradiating and laser_length to disk. The reflector saves its visible beam, age, length and irradiating state. All of these are recomputed on the next tick (pathDirty=true), and the reflector clamps the loaded values with Math.max even though the game only produces non-negative values. LaserBeam's compact constructor also throws on negative values the game never produces.
issues.reason: Runtime display state does not need to be saved, and the extra validation guards states the game cannot produce, which the code style forbids.
issues.fix: Save only inventory and energy in saveAdditional, and send irradiating, laser_length and the visible beam only through getUpdateTag. Remove the Math.max clamps and the LaserBeam negativity check.

issues.problem: The blue beam reflected by `laser_reflector` (10,100,0 facing west) goes through the polished_deepslate target at (4,100,0) without stopping. It continues to the 32-block maximum, past the other test blocks, and ends almost at the camera (from about 840,480 down to the hotbar at the bottom right). The same overshoot shows in four-emitter-directions-front: the horizontal blue line at z=0 keeps going left of the deepslate block at about 1430–1650 px and crosses the whole frame. It also shows in red-green-crossing-and-reflector: the blue line runs past the deepslate to about 655,270 px.
issues.reason: The reflector draws its beam with the default `LaserPath(MAX_LENGTH=32)` and never uses the real path. The Tier 7 laser at (10,-5) is placed before the reflector, so its BlockEntity ticks first. Each tick `receiveLaser` sets `receivedGameTime` to the current game time and calls `sync()`. When `LaserReflectorBlockEntity.serverTick` runs later in that same tick, the check `receivedGameTime < gameTime` is false every time. As a result `LaserPath.find` never runs, the beam is never forwarded, and the client always gets `laser_length=32` with `irradiating=true`. The reflected beam is shown but stops nowhere, and its target never receives it.
issues.fix: Separate the beam received this tick from the beam sent out. In `receiveLaser`, merge into a pending beam keyed by game time. In `serverTick`, send out the pending beam from earlier ticks no matter how the BlockEntities are ordered. For example, keep `pendingBeam`/`pendingTime` and `outgoingBeam`: at tick start, when `pendingTime < gameTime`, promote pending to outgoing. Or compare against the last processed time rather than the last received time. Always run `LaserPath.find` before the first `sync()` that sets `irradiating=true`, and make the initial client `laser_length` 0 instead of `MAX_LENGTH`. Then the beam ends at the first non-air block (length 6 here) and reaches the target.

issues.problem: The only place the laser reflector is visible is a small opaque white vertical sliver (about 1840–1860 x 300–355 px) in front of the Tier 7 laser. It reads as a stray white beam or z-artifact, not as a reflector. The original translucent pale-blue reflector look is lost.
issues.reason: The `laser_reflector` model is a thin plate, 12×12×2 px (from [2,2,1] to [14,14,3]), with `render_type` `minecraft:cutout`. The original texture `laserreflector.png` is a pale, semi-transparent light-blue image. Cutout makes every pixel either fully opaque or fully discarded, so the plate renders flat white and solid. Its 2 px edge, auto-UV'd, is all you see from most angles. The cullface entries on faces that are not on the block boundary are also wrong, because those faces disappear next to solid neighbours.
issues.fix: Change the reflector model's render type to `minecraft:translucent` so the texture keeps its alpha. Make the shape match the original reflector renderer in the hotfix2 JAR (check `RenderLaserReflector` or the block's render bounds) rather than a 2 px plate, so it is visible from the side and the front. Remove `cullface` from faces that are not on the block boundary. Then regenerate with `runData`.
